newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish markets unperturbed by new Finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish markets unperturbed by new Finance minister.

text.p: Polish forex and money markets on Tuesday reacted calmly to the resignation of Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko and expect no major changes in economic policy from his replacement Marek Belka, bankers said.

Belka, an independent economist and former adviser to the Polish president, said he would continue macro-economic consolidation, with curbs on inflation and a tight budget, but markets reserved judgement on prospects for long-term success.
"Polish markets and foreign investors want to see what Belka will do, because he is relatively unknown," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, a senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Bankers said that markets would closely monitor Belka's determination to keep a lid on government spending and inflation in an election year.
"We will see if the government loosens its financial discipline with the arrival of the new Finance Minister," said one analyst at a foreign company here.
Analysts added, however, that the 1997 budget was already passed and that any possible financial loosening would not be large-scale, even with parliamentary elections due in autumn.

Dealers said foreign investors would likely take time to digest the news and may put-off further investment decisions until Belka reassures them that budget discipline would remain intact. They said local markets showed little reaction.
"Polish markets should remain basically unchanged as Kolodko's resignation seems a strictly personal move, without economic implications," said Piotr Linke, chief dealer at Creditanstalt in Warsaw.
Polish discount Bradies were flat around 98.25/98.50, signalling that foreign investors were untroubled by Kolodko's departure and remained generally bullish on Poland.
The zloty was calm in morning trade, holding flat against the basket of currencies with no large upward or downward pressure, dealers said.
They said there was some movement in T-bill yields on Tuesday not connected with Kolodko, but rather the result of short-term cash-shortage on the domestic money market.
Many Polish banks found themselves short of cash this week after starting the new monthly required reserve period with low levels, dealers said.
